The amount of damage you take is based on the voltage of the cable that shocked you. [color=green]Low Voltage[/color] cables will deal less damage than [color=Yellow]Medium Voltage[/color] cables, which will deal less damage than [color=Orange]High Voltage[/color] cables. Energized [color=Orange]High Voltage[/color] and [color=Yellow]Medium Voltage[/color] cabling hurts, so be sure to wear insulated gloves when working with it.

title: WirePanels
content: [GUÍA OFICIAL: WirePanels]: Some station devices like airlocks, vending machines, and arcade consoles have wire panels, which control certain aspects of their functionality. These panels can be opened using a screwdriver to access the wiring inside. From here you can use wirecutters and a multitool to interact with the wiring. Note that interacting with the wiring often requires insulated gloves, as if the wire is live, you can get shocked. You can cut and mend wires using the wirecutters and pulse wires using the multitool. Cutting wires often completely disables or restores functionality to a device. It may also trigger unintended functionality like shocking people, dropping door bolts, or exploding. Pulsing wires can have a variety of effects, but oftentimes it either temporarily disables or enables functionality. You can't pulse wires if the wire you're trying to pulse is cut. You have to mend the wire first.

title: AdvancedBrute - # Specialized Brute Chemicals
content: [GUÍA OFICIAL: AdvancedBrute - # Specialized Brute Chemicals]: Nanotrasen's greatest scientists have synthesized three more specific brute chemicals! Each one heals a specific damage subtype.

title: AdvancedBrute - # Specialized Brute Chemicals
content: [GUÍA OFICIAL: AdvancedBrute - # Specialized Brute Chemicals]: [color=red]USE CAUTION[/color] when using the aforementioned specialized brute chemicals. Should one mix together with a different type of brute chemical, the resulting mixture will create a dangerous chemical known as Razorium! To avoid this, make sure the patient is done metabolizing one brute medication before giving them another. Keep an eye on the rate their health is changing. [bold]Some examples of mixtures that create Razorium are as follows:[/bold] Bicaridine and Puncturase Puncturase and Lacerinol Bruizine and Bicaridine Lacerinol and Bruizine Please note that [bold]any[/bold] combination of these 4 chemicals will likely mix and create Razorium! Be careful when creating these chemicals, as they contain Bicaridine. Any leftover Bicaridine will likely mix to create Razorium!

title: Botanicals
content: [GUÍA OFICIAL: Botanicals]: Botany and Chemistry can often work together to produce better medicine (or recreational cocktails). It may be worthwhile to give them the fertilizers they need, and request some medicinal plants in return.

title: Chemist
content: [GUÍA OFICIAL: Chemist]: Now you've done it. You picked the one job where -math- is mandatory. Grab your beaker, pull up a chair, and get cracking, it's time to cook up some chems. While chemists primarily make medications, there's a very wide variety of chemicals that can be made, all of which are showcased in the Chemicals entry of the Guidebook. [textlink="Click here to see a complete list of chemicals." link="Chemicals"] For automated chemical production, see [textlink="Plumbing" link="Plumbing"].

title: Chemist
content: [GUÍA OFICIAL: Chemist]: Chemistry is fairly straightforward once you know what to expect. Here's a simple, step-by-step process on how to begin. - Grab a beaker, Pill Canister, and if desired, some Bottles. - Place the beaker in the Chemical Dispenser, and Pill Canister (or bottle) in the Chem Master. - Open the Chemical Dispenser UI, and make your mix. Recipes are in other sections of the guidebook. - Alt-click the dispenser to remove your beaker, and place it in the Chem Master. - Open the Chem Master UI. On the Input tab, move your mix into the buffer. - Move to the Output tab, customise your pill, and press the Create button. - Alt-click the Chem Master to get the pill bottle out. You may have to remove the beaker first. - Click on a table, crate, or another surface to empty the pill bottle if desired. Alternatively, store or empty it into another storage container. That's it, you've made your first set of pills! Consider checking with Medical Doctors and other crew to see what else may be requested, refilling the medical kits in medbay storage, or just experimenting! You can also use the hand labeler to organize individual bottles or bags without using the Chem Master labeling system.

title: Chemist
content: [GUÍA OFICIAL: Chemist]: Speaking of experimentation, there are a few more toy you can use when it comes to chemistry. This job requires a lot of trial and error, but it was worth mentioning that these things exist! It's up to you to figure out what to make with them.

title: Cloning
content: [GUÍA OFICIAL: Cloning]: If all else fails, patients will need to be cloned. This should only be used as a last resort, if recovery is impossible. This is most often the case when the body has started to rot, or if they have excessive amounts of damage. Cloning itself is relatively simple. (Assuming the network is set.) Just drag a body into the scanner, check the cloning console, and clone! If they've taken cellular damage, or have rotted for too long, the results can be... less than pleasant. As a note: Cloning isn't always available, and it would be best not to rely on it.

title: Cloning
content: [GUÍA OFICIAL: Cloning]: Creating a clone requires biomass, which, gruesomely, involves recycling organic material. Be it crew members without a soul, station pets, or hostile creatures that have been 'taken care of', things can often be recycled. Dragging a body onto the biomass reclaimer (with your cursor) will mulch it for re-use. If it's a crew member, it's common practice to strip the body and return departmental gear before doing such.

title: Cryogenics
content: [GUÍA OFICIAL: Cryogenics]: Cryogenics can be a bit daunting to understand, but hopefully, quick run through of this diagram, you'll learn how to work it! So, let's go over what each part does: - Air in: Air comes in here through the distro or an air tank, giving those inside something to breathe, and the freezer something to chill. - Gas pump: Limits the network pressure, so those in the tube aren't crushed. - Freezer: Chills the air, and by extension, patients in the tube, so Cryoxadone can activate. - Gas filters: Removes waste gas (Carbon Dioxide and Nitrous Oxide) from the loop. - Air out: Waste gasses go here, either into a storage tank, or into the waste network. Not every network will look like this, but hopefully, it's enough to give you the basic gist of how it's functioning. An important thing to note, winter clothing (and hardsuits) will make cryogenic treatment less, or completely ineffective. Be sure to remove cold preventative clothing before placing people in the pod.

title: Cryogenics
content: [GUÍA OFICIAL: Cryogenics]: Once things have been set up, you're going to require a specific medication, Cryoxadone. Cryoxadone heals all damage types when a patient is chilled, and can either be pre-administered (with a pill), or loaded into the cell directly with a beaker. Do note, patients won't begin to heal until they've chilled to the appropriate temperature, it may be worthwhile to wait a bit before placing a beaker inside.

title: Cryogenics - ## Additional Information:
content: [GUÍA OFICIAL: Cryogenics - ## Additional Information:]: The standard pressure for a gas pump is 100.325 kpa. Cryoxadone works at under 170K, but it is standard practice to set the freezer to 100K for faster freezing.

title: Medical
content: [GUÍA OFICIAL: Medical]: This is the department where people go to when they're hurt, it's up to the folks working here to fix them.

title: Medical
content: [GUÍA OFICIAL: Medical]: [color=#5b97bc]Medical[/color]'s staff is made up of Medical Interns, Medical Doctors, Paramedics and Chemists. [color=#5b97bc]Medical[/color] is run by the Chief Medical Officer. Right now, medbay is divided into two different sets of care:

title: MedicalDoctor
content: [GUÍA OFICIAL: MedicalDoctor]: It's time to heal. Or at least, try to heal, anyway. Medical Doctors are the primary caretakers of every boo boo and ouchie crewmembers get on the station, be it a small scratch, or boiled skin. This guide will give you a basic outline of the treatment options you have available, triage, and other avenues of care.

title: MedicalDoctor
content: [GUÍA OFICIAL: MedicalDoctor]: There are two ways to tell what's ailing someone: Taking a scan (with a health analyzer or a medical PDA), or examining them, with a shift-click, and clicking the heart symbol. Using a health analyzer is often more powerful than examination, as some things (such as poison, or radiation) don't show up on examination. However, using an analyzer has its drawbacks, as it makes noise and uses up a battery.

title: MedicalDoctor - ## Medication and Treatment Options
content: [GUÍA OFICIAL: MedicalDoctor - ## Medication and Treatment Options]: Before we go any further, it's probably a good idea to go over damage types, and what will heal them. The wiki has more extensive info available, but these are commonly used. An important note: Most medication has an overdose level, which will cause harm to your patient. Chemicals also take time to metabolise in pill form, if you want things to act quickly, use a syringe. - Brute Damage: Bicaridine or Bruise Packs - Burn Damage: Dermaline or Ointment - Toxin (Poison): Dylovene - Toxin (Radiation) Hyronalin or Arithrazine - Airloss: Dexaline or Inaprovaline - Bloodloss: Dexaline (Examine the patient, if pale, they still need blood or iron.) - Bleeding: Tranexamic acid and Gauze (Bleeding can also be cauterized with burn damage.) Many stations are stocked with kits in storage, and all medics have some equipment in their starting belt.

title: MedicalDoctor - ## Basic Treatment and Triage
content: [GUÍA OFICIAL: MedicalDoctor - ## Basic Treatment and Triage]: Examine your patient, and note down the important details: Are they alive? Bleeding? What type of damage? If alive, treat them as best as you can. Patients are in critical condition at 100 damage, and dead at 200. Keep this in mind when choosing how to treat them. Emergency Pens and Epinephrine are often used to keep patients stable. If possible, buckle them to a medical bed, if you need time to treat them, strap them to a stasis bed instead. Just keep in mind that metabolism (and by extension, healing chemicals) are slowed to a crawl when on stasis, they'll need to be taken off of it for the medicine to be effective. (But Blood Packs, Ointment, and Brute packs all work as normal.)

title: MedicalDoctor - ## Basic Treatment and Triage
content: [GUÍA OFICIAL: MedicalDoctor - ## Basic Treatment and Triage]: You can't save them all, sometimes, death happens. Depending on the [color=#a4885c]status[/color] of the body, there are a few things that can be done. 1. Do they have a soul attached? You can tell if, when examining, the following phrase is displayed: "Their soul has departed." If this isn't displayed, there is still a player who can be revived. 2. Is the body rotting? If it is, sadly, they'll have to be cloned. A rotting body can't be brought back with a defibrillator. (See Cloning) 3. If they have a soul, and aren't rotten, it's possible to revive them. Consider storing the body in a morgue tray if you don't have enough time to revive someone, as the body will rot if you wait too long.

title: MedicalDoctor - ## Basic Treatment and Triage
content: [GUÍA OFICIAL: MedicalDoctor - ## Basic Treatment and Triage]: Not counting airloss, Defibrillator's can be used to revive patients under 200 total damage. Chemicals don't metabolise in the dead, but brute packs and ointment can still patch them up. Use them to bring their numbers down enough for revival.

content: [GUÍA OFICIAL: Medicine]: These medications are almost always useful to medbay in one way or another.

title: Arachnid
content: [GUÍA OFICIAL: Arachnid]: They have two additional Pocket slots in their inventory. They can eat raw meat without any ill effects, but some foods like chocolate and onion poisons them. They suffocate 50% faster, and their Blue Blood can't be metabolised from Iron, being based on Copper instead. Their unarmed attacks deal Piercing damage instead of Blunt.

title: Arachnid
content: [GUÍA OFICIAL: Arachnid]: Arachnids can create Websilk at the cost of getting more hungry. They (and only they) can craft bundles of websilk into various items from clothing and shields to entire walls.

title: Diona
content: [GUÍA OFICIAL: Diona]: They can't wear shoes, but are not slowed by Kudzu. They get hungry and thirsty slower. They can restore hunger by drinking certain water-based beverages. They fall into a critical state at [color=lightgreen]125[/color] points of damage. They die at [color=red]250[/color] points of damage. Their "blood" is tree sap and can't be metabolised from Iron. Being plants, Weed Killer poisons them, while Robust Harvest heals them (but not without risk when overused!) They take [color=#1e90ff]30% less Blunt damage and 20% less Slash damage[/color]; but [color=#ffa500]50% more Heat damage, 20% more Shock damage, and they can easily catch on fire when receiving enough Heat damage from *any* source, up to 5 fire stacks.[/color]

title: Diona - ## Make Like A Tree And Leave
content: [GUÍA OFICIAL: Diona - ## Make Like A Tree And Leave]: Being exposed to too much Robust Harvest will cause a Diona to grow out of control, turning into an immobile tree (dropping all their equipment). Cutting down the tree will "restore" the Diona to their mobile state.

title: Diona - ## Make Like A Tree And Leave
content: [GUÍA OFICIAL: Diona - ## Make Like A Tree And Leave]: After death, a Diona can voluntarily destroy their own body, releasing their "internal organs" as three Nymphs, with the player taking control of the Brain Nymph. It can talk but has no hands or inventory, and can't do much. After 5 minutes, a Nymph can reform into a whole Diona. This will be a new randomised body with a random name, and there will be little to no evidence beyond their word about who they were before.

title: Dwarf
content: [GUÍA OFICIAL: Dwarf]: Dwarves or Dwarfs are a stout, mostly hairless species from the planet Abumas, located near the Null Scar. Their convergent evolution toward a Human-like appearance is strong enough to result in frequent misidentification, though there are enough deep cultural and physiological differences to justify treating them as a distinct group, outside the gamut of other near-Human subspecies like half-Felionoids and half-Vulpkanin, in addition to their unique origin as a totally separate clade. Most Dwarves are male (around 87%), with the rest being female. Gender-nonconforming Dwarves are rarer than their Humans counterparts. Male Dwarves are often easily identified by their full, shaggy hair and large beards. Dwarves with no hair, including beardless males, are generally considered unusual. The average Dwarf is around 110 cm (3' 7") in height at maturity, with no significant difference between the sexes, but exhibits much fuller, denser bones and pronounced cartilaginous features compared to humans such as larger noses and cheekbones. This robustness grants them the ability to endure [color=#40ff40]10% more damage[/color] than humans before succumbing to their injuries. Xenobiologists widely agree that Dwarves evolved this stature to withstand the enhanced gravity of Abumas, which is around 1.3 times Earth standard. Dwarf society has many nuances and subdivisions, and no two Dwarf settlements are truly the same, but ethnographers have long noted a general tendency toward certain parallels with the Nordic, Celtic, and Germanic cultures of Earth in terms of their material culture. The primary weapon wielded by Dwarves during their Iron Age was the battle-ax, followed by the war-pick and war-hammer, with relatively little emphasis on spears, bows, and swords; surviving specimens tend to be highly engraved with knot patterns and runes. The major Dwarf ethnic groups are named according to their favored biomes: Subterranean Dwarves, Deepdwarves, Steppedwarves, Oceandwarves, Spiredwarves, Mountain Dwarves, Jungle Dwarves, and Forest Dwarves. Dwarves have long been a space-faring race. Their homeworld of Abumas lacks significant rare earth mineral deposits near the surface, resulting in a monopoly on these resources by the Deepdwarves. To break this monopoly, they surface-dwelling Dwarves began mining asteroids and planetoids as a workaround. These space settlements, usually called Citadels, begin their lives as simple mining outposts. As they attract more families and workers, the outposts, homes, and businesses, expand into the shafts and tunnels, eventually forming splendid cities with diverse economies and populations. A fully-developed Citadel is a massive ark that can fly under its own power, though the majority of asteroid mines are abandoned once the minerals run out and never achieve this glory. Particularly impressive or culturally significant Citadels are often landed on planets to serve as museums or palaces, and there is a thriving industry of using grounded Citadels to stake a claim on newly-colonized worlds, as a 'readymade city' that can be deployed in an afternoon. Abumas's proximity to the Null Scar inevitably meant that Dwarves would come in contact with NanoTrasen. Several Citadels now have highly profitable relationships with NT, and are under direct contract to provide certain high-demand minerals to the far-flung corners of Starlight Sector, beyond the reach of the Corporation's logistical network.

title: Dwarf
content: [GUÍA OFICIAL: Dwarf]: To most species, alcohol is a poisonous but highly entertaining beverage valued for its euphoric and sedative effects. This is only partly true for Dwarves, who have a [color=#1e90ff]physiological need for alcohol[/color], much like Humans need dietary fat to remain healthy; it is a critical macronutrient. To a Dwarf, [color=#1e90ff]alcoholic drinks also satiate hunger[/color], and [color=#1e90ff]food is less effective at satiating hunger[/color]. Moreover, [color=#ff901e]pure water is intolerable and causes vomiting[/color]. More importantly, Dwarves often have odd reactions to certain beverages. Some of these peculiar interactions are described below. The following drinks grant benefits directly from the tap, without any further mixing: Water equivalent to Ipecac (causes vomiting) Ale restores thirst; no Ethanol Beer restores hunger Mead equivalent to Tricordazine Vodka equivalent to Hyronalin Whiskey 10% less Blunt damage taken Rum 10% less Slash damage taken Absinthe 10% less Piercing damage taken Tequila 10% less Heat damage taken Cognac 10% less Cold damage taken Gin 10% less Caustic damage taken Vermouth 10% less Shock damage taken
