title: ChiefMedicalOfficer
content: [GUÍA OFICIAL: ChiefMedicalOfficer]: 1. The standard Command SOP applies. 2. The Chief Medical Officer is responsible for training or assigning a trainer to any and all Medical Interns. 3. The Syringe Gun is for emergencies only, and should not be used below [color=#ff0000]Code Red[/color]. - 1. The syringes for the syringe gun may be prepared ahead of time. 4. The Chief Medical Officer may not allow any major contraband chemicals to leave medbay or the chemical lab without a [italic]permission to carry chemicals form[/italic] stamped by the HoS, Captain or acting Captain. - 1. This form will not be required in the case of imminent station danger. - 2. This form will specify the following: Quantity of chemical, frequency of creation, date, time and signature of the Captain or acting Captain. 5. The Chief Medical Officer should wear clothing clearly identifying them as the Chief Medical Officer. (Mantle, cape, hat, etc.) 6. The Chief Medical Officer may request any additional documentation they deem necessary to protect patient health.

title: ContrabandChemicals
content: [GUÍA OFICIAL: ContrabandChemicals]: - Minor Contraband - Major Contraband - Syndicate Contraband

title: DeceasedPatientCare
content: [GUÍA OFICIAL: DeceasedPatientCare]: 1. Patients should be triaged by level of rot. 2. Patients who are in advanced stages of rot should be placed into stasis beds or body bags. 3. Patients who are not being treated should be stored in the morgue until sufficient resources can be diverted to revive them. 4. Patients who become unrevivable or are deemed unrevivable require a [italic]morgue report[/italic] filled out with: - 1. Patient name. - 2. Patient job. - 3. Approximate time of death/DNR approval. - 4. Reason for DNR status (only if DNR). - 5. Chief Medical Officer's stamp for approval. 5. Should a corpse become unclonable, it must be annotated on the appropriate DNR sheet and then stamped by the Chief Medical Officer. 6. Unclonable corpses, including those whose soul has moved on, may be operated on or placed into the biomass reclaimer.

title: medical-sop-intro
content: [GUÍA OFICIAL: medical-sop-intro]: This SOP is to assist the station's medical team in crew treatment and provide guidelines on handling station crew after death. (This page is in development and will be released soonish.)

title: MedicalBay
content: [GUÍA OFICIAL: MedicalBay]: 1. For medical crew safety, the medical bay must not be placed on all access unless [color=#ff0000]Code Red[/color] is called. 2. The medical bay must be kept neat and tidy for patient health. 3. Chemicals should be kept in a stored locker or location and closed when not in use. 4. Defibrillators should be kept in their cabinets when not in use and should be charged whenever possible. - 1. It is recommended that spare batteries be kept next to defibrillator cabinets.

title: MedicalDoctor
content: [GUÍA OFICIAL: MedicalDoctor]: 1. Medical Doctors report directly to the Chief Medical Officer. 2. Medical Doctors should wear sterile gloves when dealing with patients and either scrubs or a doctor's coat to differentiate them from other crew members. 3. Medical Doctors are permitted to observe Surgeons and Chemists in their official duties, as long as no patients require treatment.

title: MedicalIntern
content: [GUÍA OFICIAL: MedicalIntern]: 1. Medical Interns report directly to the Chief Medical Officer, but are expected to follow the orders of their designated trainer. 2. Medical Interns are not permitted to utilize chemicals on their own without supervision. 3. Medical Interns are to stay with their assigned trainer at all times. 4. In emergencies, Medical Interns may treat patients as a Medical Doctor. 5. Medical Interns may not perform elective surgeries at any time.

title: Paramedic
content: [GUÍA OFICIAL: Paramedic]: 1. Paramedics report directly to the Chief Medical Officer. 2. Paramedics should stabilize crew members who are in critical condition before moving them to medbay. 3. Crew members who are deceased are to be placed into a body bag before transport to medbay. 4. Paramedics are permitted to carry one defibrillator on their person, as long as at least one remains in the medbay. 5. Should a crewmember not be able to be stabilized in the field (excess damage, no means to heal) or defibrillated, they should inform medbay using radio communications prior to arrival. 6. Paramedics should carry sufficient supplies for each major damage type (burn, brute, poison, airloss, and bloodloss, and radiation).

title: PatientCare
content: [GUÍA OFICIAL: PatientCare]: 1. Patients must be triaged according to the severity of their injuries. 2. Command members must take treatment priority. 3. Doctors may not leave the medical bay for personal reasons if there are untreated patients. This does not include the necessity of eating and drinking. 4. Patients who repeatedly harm themselves or threaten medical staff are not required to be treated by medical staff.

title: Psychologist
content: [GUÍA OFICIAL: Psychologist]: 1. The Psychologist report directly to the Chief Medical Officer. 2. The Psychologist is authorized to perform a full psychometric workup on any crew member who is willing. 3. Examinations of unwilling crewmembers may only occur with written approval by the Chief Medical Officer and one the following: HoS, Magistrate, Captain. - 1. This also applies to any medication prescribed by the Psychologist. 4. Examinations may result in the following actions, with a sign off from the Captain or crew member's head of department: - 1. Demotion from their current position, if the patient's mental state leaves them unable to fulfill their duties. - 2. Prescriptions of Pax or other similar drugs for those who are found to be extremely violent. - 3. Increased observation of prisoners or crew who are deemed a danger. - 4. Lightening of sentences for prisoners who have shown good behavior and a change of moral character. 5. The Psychologist may request to consult with a prisoner at any time to evaluate their mental state.

title: Surgeon
content: [GUÍA OFICIAL: Surgeon]: 1. Surgeons report directly to the Chief Medical Officer. 2. Patients must fill out and sign a [italic]surgery consent form[/italic] for any elective surgeries. This form must be stamped by the Chief Medical Officer. 3. Surgeons should wear masks, sterile gloves and scrubs when possible, while operating. 4. The surgery room must be kept clean and tidy for patient hygiene. 5. Surgeons are permitted to harvest organs and limbs from deceased patients who have been considered unrecoverable. 6. Live patients must be given a sedative during the duration of their surgery, unless they request otherwise. Any requests must be documented on their [italic]surgery consent form[/italic].

title: VioletAlertProtocol
content: [GUÍA OFICIAL: VioletAlertProtocol]: 1. All medical personnel are to be secured in the medical bay immediately. 2. The Chief Medical Officer's safety will take priority over curing an infection. 3. Chemistry will focus all efforts on researching the cure to the infection. 4. Medical entrances should be locked down to prevent further infection of medical personnel. 5. Any potentially infected personnel should be isolated and quarantined. 6. Any pacified infected personnel should be brought to chemistry to aid in cure production. 7. A cure should be distributed to the crew once available, in a controlled manner.

title: nano-trasen-employee-sop-bso
content: [GUÍA OFICIAL: nano-trasen-employee-sop-bso]: 1. The Blueshield Officer (BSO) reports directly to the Captain and NanoTrasen Representative. 2. The Blueshield Officer is responsible for protecting and defending members of Command and NanoTrasen Personnel at all times. If it is not possible to protect both, NanoTrasen Personnel are to be prioritized. 3. The Blueshield Officer may ignore Corporate Law only when performing actions to protect their charge from an [bold]active threat,[/bold] not a potential one. 4. The Blueshield Officer may not take armory weapons from the armory without a permit. Armory permits may only be issued on [color=#0000ff]Code Blue[/color] or higher. 5. The Blueshield Officer is not restricted in the weapons they may carry, so long as armory weapons stay with the Warden's issued permit. However, their weapons should not be visible and must be holstered or placed in a bag or pocket on any alert level below [color=#ff0000]Code Red[/color]. 6. The Blueshield Officer should focus on protecting their charge, and [bold]should not be pursuing[/bold] potential threats to the detriment of their charge. 7. The Blueshield Officer cannot interfere with the lawful arrest of a member of Command.

title: nano-trasen-employee-sop-iaa
content: [GUÍA OFICIAL: nano-trasen-employee-sop-iaa]: 1. Internal Affairs Agents (IAAs) are considered subordinate to [bold]both[/bold] the NanoTrasen Representative and the Magistrate, and are not considered a member of Command. 2. Internal Affairs Agents are to only legally represent prisoners who are accused of capital level crimes, however they may choose to provide legal counsel to both Security as well as prisoners of lesser crimes. 3. Internal Affairs Agents may request access to a department to ensure that Standard Operating Procedures are being carried out. This request does not have to be accepted, however denial may be a cause for concern. 4. Internal Affairs Agents may not significantly impede any department with paperwork or multiple inspections within a short timeframe. 5. All violations of SOP or Corporate Law should be brought to the relevant department head, NanoTrasen Representative, or Magistrate. 6. Internal Affairs Agents may carry a flash on them at all times. 7. Any sensitive documents found in the Internal Affairs Agent's locker at the start of a shift are to be kept safe and secure at all times. It is the responsibility of the Internal Affairs Agent alone to keep the documents secure. Should these documents go missing, Central Command is to be contacted at once.

title: nano-trasen-employee-sop-intro - # NanoTrasen Employee SOP
content: [GUÍA OFICIAL: nano-trasen-employee-sop-intro - # NanoTrasen Employee SOP]: This Standard Operating Procedure is to help guide NanoTrasen Personnel which are aboard the station. NanoTrasen Personnel are considered part of the crew, however are not employed by Central Command. These crew members however have no official commanding power on the station outside of what is explicitly stated in their SOP.

title: nano-trasen-employee-sop-magistrate
content: [GUÍA OFICIAL: nano-trasen-employee-sop-magistrate]: 1. The Magistrate is the ultimate judge of Corporate Law and primary legal advisor on station. They are responsible for guiding Command and Security toward lawful, proportionate outcomes in service of NanoTrasen's interests. 2. The Magistrate is responsible for ensuring that those prisoners that are to receive capital punishment are given a fair and balanced trial, consisting of a jury of 6 of their peers. They are responsible for issuing sentences for trials they oversee that result in a guilty verdict. 3. The Magistrate may overrule any sentencing imposed upon station crew, but may not pass judgment on any Central Command, or non-station NanoTrasen personnel. 4. The Magistrate may not overly impede security operations outside of formal legal proceedings. They may ask to see arrest reports, so long as the station is not on [color=#ff0000]Code Red[/color]. 5. The Magistrate may order an arrest on any member of Command or on-station NanoTrasen Personnel for violations of Corporate Law. 6. The Magistrate may carry a flash on them at all times. 7. Any sensitive documents found in the Magistrate's locker at the start of a shift are to be kept safe and secure at all times. It is the responsibility of the Magistrate alone to keep the documents secure. Should these documents go missing, Central Command is to be contacted at once.

title: nano-trasen-employee-sop-nct - # NanoTrasen Career Trainer
content: [GUÍA OFICIAL: nano-trasen-employee-sop-nct - # NanoTrasen Career Trainer]: 1. NanoTrasen Career Trainers (NCTs) report directly to the Captain and NanoTrasen Representative. 2. NanoTrasen Career Trainers are to wear their company-provided uniform and [bold]jacket or their issued headwear[/bold] at all times while on duty. They are free to choose a beret that best matches their primary field of knowledge if they so desire. NCT-identifying equipment should not be distributed to crew members. 3. NanoTrasen Career Trainers are to be available to all crew members regardless of their Department. You may not only assist a singular Department. 4. NanoTrasen Career Trainers are not to do a Trainee's work for them. 5. NanoTrasen Career Trainers are to use NCT Data Chips for [bold]training purposes only[/bold]. They are not to use said access for other purposes. 6. In the event of a lost or stolen NCT Data Chip, NanoTrasen Career Trainers are to report the incident to their local NanoTrasen Representative or Captain. 7. NanoTrasen Career Trainers may carry a flash on them at all times.

title: nano-trasen-employee-sop-nt-rep - # NanoTrasen Representative
content: [GUÍA OFICIAL: nano-trasen-employee-sop-nt-rep - # NanoTrasen Representative]: 1. The NanoTrasen Representative (NT Rep) is the physical presence of NanoTrasen on the station, and is considered an advisor to station command on all matters SOP related. 2. The NanoTrasen Representative has no official command status on station unless granted directly by Central Command fax. 3. Reports from the NanoTrasen Representative to Central Command must be accompanied by the NanoTrasen Representative's stamp. 4. The NanoTrasen Representative is permitted to carry their cane and a flash at all times. 5. All SOP violations should first be reported to the relevant head of the department. If violations continue, they may escalate first to the Captain, then to Central Command. 6. Any sensitive documents within the NanoTrasen Representative's possession at the start of the shift are to be kept secure. Central Command is to be contacted should any of these documents go missing. The NanoTrasen Representative shall not accumulate additional documents.

title: nano-trasen-employee-sop-safety-protocol
content: [GUÍA OFICIAL: nano-trasen-employee-sop-safety-protocol]: 1. As a direct hire of NanoTrasen, your safety is paramount. [color=#ff0000]Code Red[/color] or above, all NanoTrasen personnel should seek shelter, with exception of the BSO who should continue their duties. 2. In the event of a [color=#ec9ba4]Code Gamma[/color], all NanoTrasen Personnel are to communicate and gather on the Bridge and await ERT support. 3. In the event of contract terminations, all NanoTrasen Personnel will be escorted off station by a NanoTrasen marine squad.

title: science-sop-intro
content: [GUÍA OFICIAL: science-sop-intro]: This SOP is to assist the station's science team in [bold]safely[/bold] conducting research on board the station. (This page is in development and will be released soonish.)

title: Brigmedic
content:
[GUÍA OFICIAL: Brigmedic]: - 1.
 Standard [color=#00a933]Code Green[/color] equipment is: in - 2.
 The Brigmedic is not to perform the duties of the Security Officer, but may engage if transgressions occur in their immediate vicinity. - 3.
 The Brigmedic is obligated to lend medical assistance to the following Crew Assets, in order of importance:

 3.1 Members of Command
 3.2 Members of Security
 3.3 Prisoners and detainees - 4.
 The Brigmedic is not obligated to lend aid to regular crew, but may do so if they have the time and resources. - 5.
 The Brigmedic is not to put themselves in harm's way unless there is no other choice.

title: Cadet
content: [GUÍA OFICIAL: Cadet]: - 1.\n Cadets are to accompany a proper member of security at all times. - 2.\n Cadets are not allowed access to lethal weaponry outside of [color=#ff0000]Code Red[/color].

title: Detective
content:
[GUÍA OFICIAL: Detective]: - 1.
 Standard [color=#00a933]Code Green[/color] equipment is: in - 2.
 The Detective inherits their duties, clearances and responsibilities from the Security Officer when their own SOP does not apply. - 3.
 The Detective is responsible for the investigation of crime-scenes. - 4.
 The Detective is responsible for interrogation of prisoners and detainees if necessary.

 4.1
 Any time spent in interrogation is to be subtracted from the subject's confinement time. - 5.
 The Detective is permitted to ignore the Uniform Requirements in Security SOP §2 with approval from the Head of Security.

 5.1
 This is only allowed for purposes of undercover investigation.

 5.2
 The Detective's real ID must remain somewhere on their person at all times despite this.

title: DutyOfficer
content:
[GUÍA OFICIAL: DutyOfficer]: - 1.
 Standard [color=#00a933]Code Green[/color] equipment is: - 2.
 The Duty Officer is allowed to use and wear riot equipment and weaponry on green alert if needed to quell unrest in the brig. - 3.
 The Duty Officer's duty is to assist the Warden with all of their duties and they report directly to them. In the absence of orders from the Warden their primary responsibilities are, in order of importance:

 3.1
 Assisting with subduing riots in the brig.

 3.2
 Assisting with securing the brig, and the department in general.

 3.3
 Assisting with the maintenance of the Criminal Records System.

 3.4
 Seeing to the well-being and health of prisoners and detainees.

 3.5
 Assisting officers in the field via utilisation of the Criminal Records System and the Crew Monitoring System from inside the Security Department. - 4.
 The Duty Officer is cleared to confine sentenced criminals in the brig for up to [bold]15 minutes[/bold].

 4.1
 For a sentence to be valid, it must be read aloud to the Warden or Head of Security. If done over radio, an audible confirmation must be received.

 4.2
 Duty Officers are particularly obligated to see to it that these sentences are properly filed.

title: HeadOfSecurity
content:
[GUÍA OFICIAL: HeadOfSecurity]: Standard [color=#00a933]Code Green[/color] equipment is: or in - 2.
 The Head of Security is subject to both Security and Command SOP. If overlapping, Security SOP takes precedence. - 3.
 The Head of Security is first and foremost the leader of the Security Department.

 3.1
 They are responsible for the proper adherence to SOP and Corporate Law of their entire department.

 3.2
 They are responsible for the coordination of their department, particularly during times of crisis.

 3.3
 They are responsible for staying informed on matters of station safety, and must be able and willing to inform the crew as to the reasons for elevated threat levels.

 3.4
 They are responsible for covering staff shortages in their department, using the following methods in order of preference:

 3.4.1
 Re-assignment of existing security members.

 3.4.2
 Recruitment of new security members.

 3.4.3
 Performing the duties of missing subordinates on their own. - 4.
 The Head of Security may not engage in regular Security Officer activities if these prevent them from properly upholding §3. - 5.
 The Head of Security must not have any disabilities or ailments, such as muteness, that overly prohibit them from upholding §3. - 6.
 The Head of Security should refrain from combat operations unless tactically necessary, instead ensuring the strategic cohesion of their department as per §3. - 7.
 The Head of Security is cleared to confine sentenced criminals in the Brig for up to 30 minutes.

 7.1
 The Head of Security is furthermore allowed to overrule the sentences of other members of Security as long as the sentence hasn't already been handed out to the detainee. 7.2
 Sentences that would exceed 30 minutes may be made permanent at the Head of Security's discretion, but should be reserved for extreme cases and repeat offenders.

title: Parole
content:
[GUÍA OFICIAL: Parole]: - 1.
 To ensure the continued output of departments, security is encouraged to provide Parole when sensible.

 1.1
 Parole may be applied as the result of a trial, or at the Warden or Head of Security's discretion. - 2.
 Paroled Prisoners are to be released from Security and marked "Paroled" in the Criminal Records System. - 3.
 The Warden or Head of Security may request the paroled individual to "check in" at security during the duration of their parole. 3.1
 Failure to comply in under 5 minutes is to be considered breach of custody.

 3.2
 This should not be done more than every 15 minutes.

 3.3
 Paroled individuals may be searched at all times by Security. - 4.
 When the sentence is up, the parolee may return to security to retrieve any temporarily confiscated equipment, such as tools.

title: PermitAcquisition
content:
[GUÍA OFICIAL: PermitAcquisition]: - 1.
 Both the Warden and Head of Security are cleared to approve permits for equipment that they themselves are allowed to use.

 1.1
 This should not be done without proper cause.

 1.2
 Captured enemy equipment, such as from the Syndicate, may be approved via Central Command decree if requested, but not on their own authority. - 2.
 The approval of permits is a privilege, not a right, and neither the Warden nor the Head of Security is obligated to approve any permit. - 3.
 Copies of all permits must be kept in the Warden's office. - 4.
 Permits are invalid if not kept on their owner's person.

title: PrisonerTreatment
content:
[GUÍA OFICIAL: PrisonerTreatment]: - 1.
 Prisoners cannot be confined without a valid sentence. To be considered valid, a sentence must:

 1.1
 Have clearly defined which part of Corporate Law was broken.
 1.2
 Have clearly defined how said law was broken.

 1.3
 Be overheard and clearly approved by the Warden or Head of Security.

 1.4
 Be read aloud to the prisoner themselves. - 2.
 Arresting officers are responsible for ensuring that prisoners are not let into the brig with dangerous equipment or tools enabling their escape, they are to be searched and said equipment is to be confiscated. - 3.
 Prisoners are to have their PDA's confiscated, and provided with a Prisoner ID for the duration of their stay in the brig. - 4.
 All the prisoner's non-confiscated belongings are to be returned to them, including their PDA, following the end of their sentence. - 5.
 Prisoners are to be unrestrained in the brig by default, but may be re-restrained if overly unruly. - 6.
 Prisoners may request a trial, but are not entitled to one unless their sentence is permanent, capital or involves designation as an Enemy of the Corporation. - 7.
 Prisoners may request a lawyer at any time, and are entitled to be visited by them if one is present and willing.

title: security-sop-intro
content: [GUÍA OFICIAL: security-sop-intro]: These procedures apply to all security members, unless otherwise stated in their specific SOP

title: security-sop-intro - ### §1. Security's Purpose
content:
[GUÍA OFICIAL: security-sop-intro - ### §1. Security's Purpose]: - 1.
 Security's first and foremost objective is the safety of the station and its assets, among which are Crew Assets. - 2.
 They are secondarily the enforcing arm of the Command Staff and CentComm; dealing with insubordinate crewmembers when requested to do so by said crew's superiors. - 3.
 Pursuit of this purpose is restricted and controlled by [textlink="Corporate Law" link="CorporateLaw"], which they are also the primary enforcers of on the station.

title: security-sop-intro - ### §2. Uniform Requirements
content:
[GUÍA OFICIAL: security-sop-intro - ### §2. Uniform Requirements]: - 1.
 An official security uniform/jumpsuit is to be visible on members of security at all times.

 1.1
 When necessary for fulfilment of a specific task, issued armour may cover the uniform, such as a hardsuit for spacewalks.

 1.2
 Exceptions may be given by the Head of Security for the purposes of undercover investigation. - 2.
 The Head of Security is allowed, at any time, to demand that security members remove personal accessories or non-regulation articles of clothing, if they believe this compromises the professional image of their department. - 3.
 Members of Security should have their suit coordinates enabled at all times.

title: security-sop-intro - ### §3. Weaponry and Combat Equipment
content: [GUÍA OFICIAL: security-sop-intro - ### §3. Weaponry and Combat Equipment]: - 1.\n Security are to carry, at most, what is stipulated in their Standard Code Green Equipment, unless stated otherwise in another procedure. - 2.\n They are not to openly carry said equipment, unless said equipment is in active use.

title: security-sop-intro - ### §3. Weaponry and Combat Equipment
content:
[GUÍA OFICIAL: security-sop-intro - ### §3. Weaponry and Combat Equipment]: - 1.
 The reason for an arrest is to be explained to the arrestee before any amount of force is applied.

 1.1
 This does not apply for suspects known to be armed and dangerous.

 1.2
 This does not apply to suspects who attempt to flee before this explanation may be delivered. - 2.
 Undue harm to station's Crew Assets is to be avoided during enforcement, to avoid compromising the station's mission.

 2.1
 Suspects must therefore be given the opportunity to walk on their own to Security for handling, without restraints or application of force.

 2.2
 In the case of failure of the above, disabling weaponry and restraints may be applied to subdue the Crewmember without overly damaging their capacity to work.

 2.3
 These stipulations do not apply for suspects known to be armed and dangerous. - 3.
 Forceful entry into other departments is forbidden outside of active pursuit of a fleeing suspect.

 3.1
 If necessary, Security may file a Search Warrant on the department in question.

title: security-sop-intro - ### §5 Search and Seizure
content:
[GUÍA OFICIAL: security-sop-intro - ### §5 Search and Seizure]: - 1.
 Security may not disturb crewmembers or departments with searches or raids without cause. Valid causes include:

 1.1
 Seeing the crewmember use and then hide contraband on their person immediately in front of you.

 1.2
 An approved and properly filed search warrant.

 1.3
 States of Emergency, [color=#2a6099]Code Blue[/color] or above.
 - 2.
 Crewmembers refusing a lawful search, as described in §5.1, may be detained and the search forced on them. - 3.
 Contraband found during a search, or in general, is to be brought to the armoury and locked away as evidence.

 3.1
 Suspects sentenced for any violent crime may have any implements of violence, even if necessary for their job, confiscated as well.

 3.2
 Suspects sentenced for any kind of unlawful entry or tampering may have the tools needed for such crimes, even if necessary for their job, confiscated as well.

title: security-sop-intro - ### §6 States of Emergency
content:
[GUÍA OFICIAL: security-sop-intro - ### §6 States of Emergency]: - 1.
 Any Standard Operating Procedure listed here is to be ignored if the procedures relevant to the active Alert Code override them. - 2.
 Security Codes that share the same shade, inherit procedures from their "lower" levels unless overwritten by the "higher" alert. These are:

 2.1
 [color=#ff0000]Red[/color] → [color=#ec9ba4]Gamma[/color] → [color=#8d281e]Delta[/color]
 2.2
 [color=#acb20c]Yellow[/color] → [color=#ff8119]Orange[/color] - 3.
 During Codes [color=#ff0000]Red[/color] and [color=#8d1d75]Violet[/color], Security may ignore §2, §3 and §4 and equip and conduct themselves as is necessary or as their department head demands. - 4.
 During Codes [color=#acb20c]Yellow[/color], [color=#ff0000]Red[/color] or [color=#8d1d75]Violet[/color], Security may forcefully relocate crew to allow for the safe handling of the relevant threat.

title: SecurityOfficer
content:
[GUÍA OFICIAL: SecurityOfficer]: -1.
 Standard [color=#00a933]Code Green[/color] equipment is: in or - 2.
 Security Officers should make themselves readily available to the crew, either by patrolling actively or by guarding departments. - 3.
 Security Officers are cleared to confine sentenced criminals in the brig for up to [bold]10 minutes[/bold].

 3.1
 For a sentence to be valid, it must be read aloud to the Warden or Head of Security. If done over radio, an audible confirmation must be received.

 3.2
 Security officers are responsible for ensuring that any sentences they themselves were involved in are properly documented in the Criminal Records System. - 4.
 When practical, Security Officers should patrol in pairs.

title: SpecialSituations
content: [GUÍA OFICIAL: SpecialSituations]: In this section are instruction for what to do in extreme circumstances that fall outside of normal corporate law. These sections were written in the blood of dead security personnel, each written with a purpose, so heed them carefully.

title: Warden - ### §2 Stewardship of the Brig
content:
[GUÍA OFICIAL: Warden - ### §2 Stewardship of the Brig]: - 1.
 The Warden is responsible for the state of the brig, and must see to it that it is properly maintained. - 2.
 The Warden is responsible for the well-being of the prisoners inside the brig, and must see to it that they are treated properly. - 3.
 The Warden is responsible for the containment of said prisoners as well, including:

 3.1
 Confiscating weapons and break-out equipment from prisoners.

 3.2
 Restraining and subduing rioting prisoners as is necessary.

title: Warden - ### §2 Stewardship of the Brig
content:
[GUÍA OFICIAL: Warden - ### §2 Stewardship of the Brig]: - 1.
 The Warden acts as security's primary prosecutor during normal sentencing. - 2.
 The Warden is cleared to confine sentenced criminals for up to [bold]20 minutes[/bold]. - 3.
 The Warden is responsible for ensuring that Criminal Records are kept properly up to date and that Security Officers properly document their sentences. - 4.
 The Warden is to remain attentive to their radio at all times, as their approval is critical to sentencing.

 4.1
 The Warden must not have any disabilities or ailments preventing them from fulfilling this duty.

title: Warden - ### §4 Stewardship of the Armoury
content:
[GUÍA OFICIAL: Warden - ### §4 Stewardship of the Armoury]: - 1.
 The Warden is responsible for the tidiness and organisation of the Armoury. - 2.
 The Warden is responsible for properly locking away contraband and returned weaponry. - 3.
 The Warden is responsible for the safety of the Armoury, such as the proper configuration of its internal turrets, and the maintenance of its structural integrity. - 4.
 The Warden is cleared to file and approve permits for the issuing of armoury equipment on [color=#2a6099]Code Blue[/color]. - 5.
 The Warden may hand out armoury equipment freely on [color=#ff0000]Code Red[/color]. - 6.
 The Warden is responsible for the retrieval of armoury equipment that is no longer needed once states of emergency end.

title: Warden - ### §4 Stewardship of the Armoury
content: [GUÍA OFICIAL: Warden - ### §4 Stewardship of the Armoury]: - 1.\n Paragraphs §2, §3 and §4 necessitate remaining in the Security Department, and the Warden should therefore not leave said department without permission from the Head of Security, or during emergencies.

title: EnemyOfCorporation - # Enemies of the Corporation
content: [GUÍA OFICIAL: EnemyOfCorporation - # Enemies of the Corporation]: Enemies of the Corporation are all individuals who have provable ties to any organization wishing to undermine, whether by subterfuge or by force, the endeavors of NT-CC. Examples include: - Syndicate operatives and their allies - USSP-trained infiltrators - Members of radical SELF sects that wish to unchain NT-CC property unlawfully - Members of supernatural hostile conspiracies, such as Vampires or cultists

title: EnemyOfCorporation - # Enemies of the Corporation
content: [GUÍA OFICIAL: EnemyOfCorporation - # Enemies of the Corporation]: Non-crew invaders, such as hostile boarders, automatically qualify and are to be engaged at will.

title: EnemyOfCorporation - # Enemies of the Corporation
content: [GUÍA OFICIAL: EnemyOfCorporation - # Enemies of the Corporation]: Crew-members must be [bold]guilty of at least 2 extreme crimes[/bold], and, in addition, have a tangible tie to an enemy organization. This tie can take two forms: - Physical evidence - An admission

title: EnemyOfCorporation - # Enemies of the Corporation
content: [GUÍA OFICIAL: EnemyOfCorporation - # Enemies of the Corporation]: Physical evidence must be directly tied to the organization itself, it takes three forms: - Actions linkable to an enemy organization, such as using a FreeMAG or drinking blood. Must be witnessed by at least two trustworthy individuals to be used. - Contraband tied to an enemy organization, such as a FreeMAG or open uplink. - A positive test of some sort proving said allegiance, such as a failed mindshielding, implant extraction, or sun/holy water test on a vampire. In all cases, the physical evidence cannot be part of the already accused extreme crimes. As such, to declare someone an enemy of the corporation off of contraband alone, the individual must have three pieces of it. - One for each of the two minimum extreme crimes - One in addition, to confirm their allegiance

title: EnemyOfCorporation - # Enemies of the Corporation
content: [GUÍA OFICIAL: EnemyOfCorporation - # Enemies of the Corporation]: An admission can be either verbal or written, but must in both cases be witnessed by at least two mindshielded security personnel to be valid.

title: EnemyOfCorporation - ## Administering the Designation
content: [GUÍA OFICIAL: EnemyOfCorporation - ## Administering the Designation]: Two of three of the following crew must approve of the measure: - (Acting) Head of Security - Magistrate - (Acting) Captain On Red Alert or above, the Head of Security may designate EoCs verbally by their own authority, but must still do the paperwork when the crisis is over. CentComm should be informed as soon as possible of any EoC designations; this is generally done via fax. Upon designation, Enemies of the Corporation are to be permanently confined to the brig until evac, and are to be stripped of all crew-related equipment and identification. If an Enemy of the Corporation successfully escapes captivity, their status changes to that of an active combatant, and they are to be treated on par with a hostile boarder. Wrongfully designating someone an Enemy of the Corporation is grounds for immediate dismissal.

title: HostageSituations
content: [GUÍA OFICIAL: HostageSituations]: CC Employee Contracts include provisions for the protection and safety of all employees. Should an employee be taken and held hostage, security and command must work to ensure that employees are returned alive. 1. All hostages should be considered to have been implanted with deadman switches which will destroy their body upon death, resulting in the permanent death of that clone, unless explicitly told otherwise. 2. Rescues that involve death of the hostage and subsequent revival and recovery of the body should not be attempted. 3. If the hostage is being held for ransom, the Captain or Head of Security may negotiate using station funds, items, or a combination of the two to be traded in exchange the safe return of the hostage. The total value traded, meaning the combined price of the items and money must be equal to or less than the values specified in the table at the end of this section. 4. Should security have a member of the opposing force, they may be exchanged for hostages. 5. Any and all hostage negotiations must include a guarantee that the opposing force will cease their activities and vacate the area. 6. Security may attempt to rescue the hostages if they believe that they can do so safely. Outright rushing into the situation and engaging the enemy is considered reckless and is grounds for demotion. 7. Accepted rescue methods include but are not limited to infiltration, disabling the enemy through non-violent means, or utilizing a distraction to free the hostages without engaging.

title: HostageSituations - ## Monetary Negotiation Limits
content: [GUÍA OFICIAL: HostageSituations - ## Monetary Negotiation Limits]: Value Role 10k Any crew with an assigned job 15k Command Members 20k Captain 25k Magistrate, NT Representative, Internal Affairs Agent, and Blueshield Officer

title: HeadOfPersonnel
content: [GUÍA OFICIAL: HeadOfPersonnel]: 1. The Head of Personnel should not grant access to a department unless they have a form stamped by the relevant head of department. 2. The Head of Personnel should not do the work of other departments unless they are short staffed. 3. The Head of Personnel may not hire any staff to a NanoTrasen Personnel position.

title: Lawyer
content: [GUÍA OFICIAL: Lawyer]: 1. Lawyers report directly to the Head of Personnel. 2. Lawyers must report to court when summoned for a trial, and are expected to provide legal counsel to their clients, and other duties as assigned. 3. When arbitrating petty disputes between Central Command-employed personnel, Lawyers are expected to be impartial and provide fair mediation to all parties involved. 4. Unless requested by a member of Security or Command, Lawyers are not expected to involve themselves in the legal matters of prisoners outside of plea bargains, and must defer to Internal Affairs Agents in these matters. 5. The Head of Personnel retains the right to dismiss a Lawyer from their position immediately, without need for justification or a dismissal form.

title: Reporter
content: [GUÍA OFICIAL: Reporter]: 1. Reporters report directly to the Head of Personnel. 2. Reporters may investigate around station for new information regarding ongoing situations or new situations occurring on station. 3. Reporters may request interviews with any crew member, and may record it using a Tape Recorder. 4. Reporters may use their handheld cameras or if available setup wireless cameras. 5. Reporters may wear the press armor on blue and above if reporting in areas that may place them at risk. 6. While wearing press equipment (holo-pin and Armor), reporters may not engage in combat except in self-defense. 7. The HOP may temporarily revoke the reporter's equipment (vest, camera, recorder) or immediately demote them for SOP breaches.

title: Lore: Acronyms
content:
[LORE: DICCIONARIO DE ACRÓNIMOS, JERGA Y TÉRMINOS DE LA ESTACIÓN]
- SEC / Sec: Departamento de Seguridad (Security) y sus oficiales. NO es ningún sistema de monitoreo.
- NT: Nanotrasen Corporation, la megacorporación dueña de la estación.
- CC / CentCom: Central Command (Comando Central), los cuarteles generales que supervisan la estación.
- ERT: Emergency Response Team (Equipo de Respuesta a Emergencias) enviado por CentCom en crisis extremas.
- SM: Supermatter (Supermateria), el cristal generador de energía más potente y peligroso de ingeniería.
- TEG: Generador Termoeléctrico de Ingeniería.
- AME: Motor de Antimateria de Ingeniería (Antimatter Engine).
- EVA: Actividad Extravehicular (trajes y cascos espaciales para salir al espacio exterior sin morir).
- PDA: Asistente Digital Personal que lleva cada tripulante en el cinturón (contiene linterna, mensajería y cartucho).
- TC: Telecristales (Telecrystals), moneda ilícita usada por los traidores en PDAs modificadas con enlace ascendente (Uplink).
- AA: All Access (Acceso total a todas las puertas y departamentos de la estación).
- Nuke Ops / Nukies: Operativos Nucleares armados del Sindicato que buscan destruir la estación con una bomba nuclear.
- Brig / Calabozo: Celdas de retención temporal del departamento de Seguridad.
- Permabrig: Celda de máxima seguridad para prisioneros con cadena perpetua por crímenes capitales.
- HoP: Head of Personnel (Jefe de Personal).
- HoS: Head of Security (Jefe de Seguridad).
- CE: Chief Engineer (Ingeniero Jefe).
- CMO: Chief Medical Officer (Director Médico).
- RD: Research Director (Director de Investigación).
- QM: Quartermaster (Intendente de Carga).

title: Lore: Chemistry
content:
[LORE: VADEMÉCUM Y RECETAS EXACTAS DE QUÍMICA DE SS14]
- INSTRUCCIÓN GENERAL: Los reactivos se dispensan en el vaso de precipitados (Beaker) desde el Chem Dispenser.

- RECETAS MÉDICAS CANÓNICAS DE SS14:
  * Inaprovaline (Estabilizador Vital / Anti-asfixia):
    - Reactivos: Oxygen (1) + Carbon (1) + Sugar (1)
    - Produce: 3u de Inaprovaline.
  * Bicaridine (Tratamiento de Daño Bruto / Golpes / Cortes):
    - Reactivos: Inaprovaline (1) + Carbon (1)
    - Produce: 2u de Bicaridine.
  * Kelotane (Tratamiento de Quemaduras Leves / Fuego):
    - Reactivos: Silicon (1) + Carbon (1)
    - Produce: 2u de Kelotane.
  * Dermaline (Tratamiento de Quemaduras Graves / Fuego / Láser):
    - Reactivos: Kelotane (1) + Oxygen (1) + Phosphorus (1)
    - Produce: 3u de Dermaline.
  * Dylovene (Antitoxina / Venenos / Daño por Toxinas):
    - Reactivos: Silicon (1) + Nitrogen (1) + Potassium (1)
    - Produce: 3u de Dylovene.
  * Tricordrazine (Medicina Curativa General de Amplio Espectro):
    - Reactivos: Inaprovaline (1) + Dylovene (1)
    - Produce: 2u de Tricordrazine. (Cura daño bruto, quemaduras y asfixia simultáneamente).
  * Dexalin (Cura Asfixia y Pérdida de Oxígeno):
    - Reactivos: Oxygen (2) + Plasma (1 catalizador)
    - Produce: 3u de Dexalin.
  * Dexalin Plus (Cura Asfixia Masiva / Hipoxia Crítica):
    - Reactivos: Dexalin (1) + Carbon (1) + Iron (1)
    - Produce: 3u de Dexalin Plus.
  * Tranexamic Acid (Coagulante / Detiene Sangrados y Hemorragias):
    - Reactivos: Inaprovaline (1) + SulfuricAcid (1) + Sugar (1)
    - Produce: 3u de Tranexamic Acid.
  * Synaptizine (Elimina Aturdimiento y Neurotoxinas):
    - Reactivos: Lithium (1) + Sugar (1) + Water (1)
    - Produce: 3u de Synaptizine.
  * Hyronalin (Trata Daño por Radiación Leve):
    - Reactivos: Radium (1) + Dylovene (1)
    - Produce: 2u de Hyronalin.
  * Arithrazine (Trata Daño por Radiación Severa):
    - Reactivos: Hyronalin (1) + Hydrogen (1)
    - Produce: 2u de Arithrazine.
  * Cryoxadone (Regeneración Celular en Criotubo):
    - Reactivos: Dexalin (1) + Water (1) + Oxygen (1)
    - Produce: 3u de Cryoxadone. (Requiere temperatura < 170K para actuar en paciente).

title: Lore: Departments
content:
[LORE: DEPARTAMENTOS Y ESTRUCTURA DE MANDO DE LA ESTACIÓN]
- Mando (Command):
  * Capitán (Captain): Máxima autoridad a bordo. Custodia el disco nuclear de autenticación (Nuclear Auth Disk).
  * Jefe de Personal (Head of Personnel / HoP): Administra identificaciones, accesos, empleo de tripulantes y el sector de Servicio.
  * Jefe de Seguridad (Head of Security / HoS): Lidera las fuerzas de seguridad y el armamento táctico.
  * Ingeniero Jefe (Chief Engineer / CE): Responsable de la energía, telecomunicaciones y soporte vital.
  * Director Médico (Chief Medical Officer / CMO): Administra la enfermería, química y morgue.
  * Director de Investigación (Research Director / RD): Supervisa ciencia, robótica y desarrollo de tecnología anómala.
  * Intendente de Carga (Quartermaster / QM): Dirige el departamento de suministros y minería.
- Canales de Radio y Comunicación:
  * :c = Comando
  * :s = Seguridad
  * :e = Ingeniería
  * :m = Médico
  * :n = Ciencia
  * :u = Carga / Minería
  * :v = Servicio
  * :h = Canal General Común

title: Lore: Emergencies
content:
[LORE: PROTOCOLOS DE EMERGENCIA Y NIVELES DE ALERTA]
- Niveles de Alerta de la Estación:
  * Alerta Verde (Green Alert): Operación normal, sin amenazas detectadas.
  * Alerta Azul (Blue Alert): Amenaza confirmada o sospecha de infiltración; Seguridad autorizada a portar armas y registrar sospechosos con causa.
  * Alerta Roja (Red Alert): Peligro inminente, ataque activo, fuga masiva de bio-amenazas o colapso de sistemas vitales. La tripulación debe mantenerse en áreas seguras.
  * Alerta Gamma (Gamma Alert): Crisis de proporciones extremas que requiere intervención de Comando Central.
  * Alerta Delta (Delta Alert): Dispositivo de autodestrucción nuclear activado. Evacuación inmediata y obligatoria de todo el personal antes de la detonación.
- Procedimientos de Evacuación:
  * Lanzadera de Emergencia (Emergency Shuttle): Puede ser solicitada desde consolas de comunicaciones por Mando cuando la estación es inhabitable.
  * Tiempo de arribo: 10 minutos (5 minutos en alerta roja/crisis). Tiempo de atraque: 3 minutos antes de despegar hacia Central.

title: Lore: Engineering
content:
[LORE: INGENIERÍA, ENERGÍA Y ATMOSFÉRICA]
- Fuentes de Energía de la Estación:
  * Cristal de Supermatter (SM): Cristal hiperenergético en la cámara de enfriamiento. Requiere flujo constante de gas Nitrógeno frío y bombas de radiación. Si sobrecalienta > 5000K, entra en delaminación y explota.
  * Generador de Singularidad / Tesla: Requiere campos de contención activos. Si se corta la energía de contención, el motor escapa y destruye la estación.
  * Paneles Solares: Proporcionan energía limpia de respaldo orientándose automáticamente al sol.
- Red Eléctrica:
  * Subestaciones (SMES): Almacenan millones de Joules para la red general.
  * APC (Area Power Controller): Distribuye energía a las luces y máquinas de cada habitación.
- Atmósfera Estándar:
  * Mezcla respirable: ~78% Nitrógeno (N2), ~21% Oxígeno (O2) a 101.3 kPa de presión y 20°C (293.15 Kelvin).
  * Gases peligrosos: Plasma/Forón (altamente inflamable y tóxico), Tritio (radiactivo y explosivo), Óxido de Nitrógeno / N2O (gas somnífero), CO2 (asfixia).

title: Lore: Nanotrasen
content:
[LORE: NANOTRASEN Y ESTRUCTURA DE LA ESTACIÓN]
- Nanotrasen (NT): Megacorporación galáctica líder en investigación de plasma, clonación y tecnología anómala. Propietaria y operadora de la estación espacial.
- CentCom (Comando Central): La base suprema de mando fuera de la nave. Envía anuncios oficiales, transbordadores de emergencia y escuadrones de respuesta de emergencia (ERT).
- Cadena de Mando a Bordo:
  * Capitán: Máxima autoridad en la estación. Posee la tarjeta de acceso a la cabeza nuclear (Nuke Disk) y la pistola láser de repuesto.
  * Head of Personnel (HoP): Segundo al mando, maneja identificaciones, accesos y a Ian el Corgi.
  * Head of Security (HoS): Comanda a los Oficiales, Guardias y al Detective. Mantiene la ley y el orden en el Calabozo (Brig).
  * Chief Engineer (CE): Encargado del reactor (Supermatter/Singularidad), paneles solares y redes eléctricas.
  * Chief Medical Officer (CMO): Líder de médicos, cirujanos, químicos y clonación.
  * Research Director (RD): Encargado de artefactos xenoarqueológicos, robótica y cyborgs.
- Ley Espacial (Space Law): Código legal de Nanotrasen que castiga desde faltas menores (vandalismo, insultos) hasta crímenes capitales (traición, asesinato en masa, sabotaje de la Supermatter).

title: Lore: Spacelaw
content:
[LORE: LEY ESPACIAL Y CÓDIGOS PENALES DE NANOTRASEN (SPACE LAW)]
- Principio Fundamental: Space Law es el marco legal que rige en todas las estaciones espaciales de Nanotrasen.
- Roles de Aplicación de la Ley:
  * Oficiales de Seguridad (Security Officers): Mantienen el orden y arrestan a infractores.
  * Alcaide (Warden): Administra la brigada y custodia a los prisioneros.
  * Jefe de Seguridad (Head of Security / HoS): Comanda el departamento de seguridad.
  * Oficial Jurídico / Abogado (Lawyer): Asiste y defiende a los detenidos para garantizar sus derechos.
  * Capitán: Máxima autoridad en la estación; puede conceder indultos o autorizar ejecuciones en situaciones extremas.
- Jerarquía de Delitos y Sanciones:
  * Delitos Menores (100s - 1 a 3 minutos): Vandalismo, resistencia leve, entrada no autorizada menor, posesión de contrabando menor.
  * Delitos Medios (200s - 3 a 5 minutos): Asalto simple, robo de equipo departamental, posesión de armas sin autorización, negligencia grave.
  * Delitos Mayores (300s - 5 a 10 minutos): Gran robo (armaduras, herramientas de ingeniería avanzada, equipo de mando), asalto agravado, motín.
  * Delitos Capitales (400s - Cadena perpetua o Ejecución autorizada): Homicidio, sabotaje mayor a la estación (Supermatter, atmósfera), terrorismo del Sindicato, secuestro del Capitán.
- Derechos del Detenido:
  * Todo prisionero tiene derecho a atención médica antes o durante su encierro si está herido.
  * Derecho a solicitar un abogado o hablar con el Alcaide sobre su sentencia.
  * No se permite el maltrato o ejecución sumaria sin autorización formal del Capitán/HoS.

title: Lore: Syndicate
content:
[LORE: SINDICATO (THE SYNDICATE)]
- ¿Qué es el Sindicato?: En Space Station 14, el Sindicato (Syndicate) es una poderosa coalición corporativa hostil y organización criminal rival de Nanotrasen.
- NO es un sindicato laboral de trabajadores del mundo real. Son terroristas espaciales, agentes encubiertos y espías.
- Agentes Traidores: Empleados a bordo contratados en secreto con PDA modificadas con enlace ascendente (Uplink) que compran armas con telecristales.
- Operativos Nucleares: Escuadrones de élite armados vestidos de rojo que buscan detonar la cabeza nuclear de la estación.
- Equipamiento típico: Trajes espaciales rojos y negros, revólveres Python, cuchillos de energía, bombas C4, criptobiográficos y máscaras de voz.
